title: Superseded and contradicted text register
statement: Unbound SHALL maintain a machine-readable register that marks every baseline record whose text is contradicted or narrowed by a convergence clause, including records the clause does not list in its amends field, and every customer-facing or assessor-facing citation SHALL resolve through that register to the governing text.
rationale: Verified examples where unamended text contradicts a governing clause: UNB-RCN-WF-005 (donee model) versus CNV-GRT-013 (agent model); UNB-PLAT-003 (Folio for all documents) versus CNV-EXP-001 (Unbound-owned PDF pipeline); RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 (dedicated database default) versus CNV-ARC-001; ACC-MDL-011 and other Strata-runtime records versus CNV-ARC-004. In addition, 59 distinct amended records are cited in this repository without their governing clause. An assessor citing the old ID receives a wrong answer.
acceptance_criteria: Every record in baseline.jsonl that a CNV clause contradicts carries a superseded_by or narrowed_by field naming the clause, verified by a script that diffs clause statements against flagged records.
The five verified contradictions listed in the rationale are flagged.
A validation check fails when an answer unit or customer document cites a flagged record without also citing its governing clause.
verification_method: Automated register check in Unbound CI plus manual review of a sample of 30 clause-record pairs.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Resolve Strata runtime persistence assumptions
statement: All Unbound requirements and architecture documents that assume Strata provides runtime append-only persistence, ordering, cryptographic integrity or tenant isolation SHALL be rewritten to the CNV-ARC-004 split (Strata for declarative schema governance; an Unbound-owned ledger component for authoritative append-only history) before architecture acceptance.
rationale: Verified: unbound@9b38de47:architecture/CONTINUOUS-CONTROL-MONITORING-AND-EVIDENCE-ASSURANCE.md line 35 states Strata is mandatory as a persistence dependency; CNV-ARC-004 assigns authoritative history to an Unbound-owned component; DD-ARC-002 found no Strata runtime typed query interface. Assessors reading the old text will expect a capability that does not exist.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed requirement is either amended to the CNV-ARC-004 split or flagged in the DD-UNB-GOV-001 register.
The continuous control monitoring architecture names the component that provides append-only history and integrity verification.
A capability verification record cites the Strata release and the PostgreSQL major versions it supports.
verification_method: Document review plus repository search showing no unflagged Strata runtime claims.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Extend the control matrix to infrastructure and security program controls
statement: The Unbound master enterprise control matrix SHALL add controls, owners and evidence definitions for network security, cloud configuration, endpoint security, encryption and key management, vulnerability management, penetration testing, personnel security and vendor management before the SOC 2 readiness assessment.
rationale: The 90 UNB-CTRL controls are all status Designed with no operating evidence, and the batch 1 infrastructure review found no network, infrastructure, cloud, endpoint or encryption controls. SOC 2 common criteria cannot be met by product controls alone.
acceptance_criteria: The matrix contains at least one control per listed domain with owner, frequency, evidence requirement ID and test procedure.
Each new control maps to at least one Trust Services Criterion.
Controls remain labeled Designed until operating evidence exists (SOC2-019).
verification_method: Control matrix review against the Trust Services Criteria mapping by the readiness assessor.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Rename or annotate the UNB-RCN prefix
statement: Unbound SHALL annotate every UNB-RCN-* record as a requirement-reconciliation record, distinct from financial reconciliation, in assessor-facing indexes.
rationale: Verified: UNB-RCN-WF, UNB-RCN-GRT, UNB-RCN-FIN, UNB-RCN-ENT and UNB-RCN-PLT records come from requirement reconciliation work; financial reconciliation is governed by CNV-FIN-004. Assessors searching for reconciliation controls are misled by the prefix.
acceptance_criteria: Assessor-facing indexes show a prefix legend distinguishing requirement reconciliation from financial reconciliation.
No answer unit cites a UNB-RCN-* record as evidence of financial reconciliation unless the record concerns money.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Counsel opinion on the regulatory perimeter
statement: Before the first sponsor activation, Echelon SHALL obtain and record a written counsel opinion on whether Unbound, as specified by CNV-LEG-001 and CNV-PAY-001, requires money transmitter licensing, investment adviser or broker-dealer registration, is a Nacha Third-Party Sender rather than a Third-Party Service Provider, or is a bank service provider, and SHALL block activation of any feature the opinion places outside the perimeter.

source_refs.locator: Third-Party Sender and Third-Party Service Provider definitions

rationale: CNV-LEG-001 labels its UPMIFA delegation analysis an interpretation. CNV-LEG-001 says Unbound SHALL NOT be able to execute a payment, and defines execute so that relaying a sponsor-authorized instruction under the sponsor delegation is not execution; UNB-XIN-REG-001 and CNV-ARC-003 describe exactly such relay at an irreversible dispatch step. The internal text is therefore consistent, but whether a bank or regulator accepts that definition is a legal question: some ODFIs may treat a file-transmitting vendor as a Third-Party Sender. Every bank-affiliated sponsor will ask this first.
acceptance_criteria: A dated opinion from licensed counsel addresses each listed regime and cites the funds-flow declaration.
The OperatorStatusRegister (UNB-XIN-REG-002) records each conclusion with its basis.
Activation of a program fails when the funds-flow conformance check finds a configuration outside the opinion.
verification_method: Legal review record plus activation gate test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Standard contract package
statement: Echelon SHALL publish, before the first sales conversation that reaches procurement, a standard contract package for Unbound consisting of a master services agreement, information security addendum, data processing agreement, service level schedule, exit and transition schedule and subprocessor terms, with a documented position on each common sponsor and bank requirement.
rationale: No Unbound requirement specifies contract artifacts beyond right-to-audit (CNV-GOV-001) and exit custody (CNV-ENT-002). Large-bank sponsors will send their own addenda; a prepared position shortens negotiation and prevents commitments the product cannot meet.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed document exists in draft reviewed by counsel.
A position matrix states accept, modify or reject for each requirement in at least three public large-bank supplier standards.
Every contractual commitment in the package maps to an Unbound requirement or a recorded owner decision.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Insurance program before production data
statement: Before any production donor data is processed, Echelon SHALL bind cyber liability (first and third party), technology errors and omissions covering financial calculation and AI-assisted output errors, and commercial crime coverage including third-party and social engineering coverage, with limits set by an adequacy analysis tied to contractual liability caps.
rationale: The Unbound baseline contains no insurance requirement (zero matches). Sponsors and banks routinely require certificates of insurance; carriers treat application answers as representations, so controls must exist before binding.
acceptance_criteria: Certificates of insurance exist for each coverage line with policy period and limits.
An adequacy analysis relates limits to liability caps in the standard contract.
Insurance application answers are reconciled to evidence before submission (EVR-INS-005).
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend). Recurring: premiums unknown; obtain quotes.

title: Contracting entity and IP title
statement: Before contracting, Echelon Foundry, LLC SHALL be formed and in good standing, SHALL hold or license all IP in Unbound and the Echelon components it uses by written assignment from every contributor, and SHALL be the entity that signs customer contracts, employs or engages personnel and holds hosting accounts.
rationale: Batch 1 found formation values all TODO in echelon-organization-administration@2763e576 and IP title unknown. No Unbound requirement covers it because it is organizational, yet every procurement process checks it first.
acceptance_criteria: A certificate of existence dated within 90 days is available.
IP assignment agreements cover every human contributor; AI-generated code ownership position is documented.
The contracting entity, IP holder and hosting account owner are the same legal entity or the relationship is documented.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Platform-generated records are customer data
statement: The standard contract SHALL define customer data to include records the platform generates about the customer, its donors, funds, grants and decisions (audit trails, decision records, acknowledgments, reconciliations and evidence), and SHALL commit to export them in the exit package.
rationale: CNV-ENT-002 makes the sponsor records custodian and requires a reconciled export, but no requirement states the contractual data definition. Batch 1 notes a competitor MSA returns only customer-provided materials; this is a differentiation point that must be contractual to count.
acceptance_criteria: The MSA data definition lists each record class in the export manifest.
The export manifest (CNV-ENT-002) covers every listed class.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Incident notification commitments by customer type
statement: Unbound SHALL define incident notification commitments per customer type: initial notice to the sponsor within 24 hours of reasonable suspicion of an incident affecting its data or service, notice to bank customers as soon as possible for incidents meeting the bank service provider rule, and notice within 72 hours to customers subject to amended Regulation S-P, each with a named channel and authenticated sender.
rationale: No Unbound requirement sets a notification time. The 24-hour target is a research recommendation pending owner decision (batch 1); the bank and Regulation S-P timings derive from those rules and apply only through the customer.
acceptance_criteria: The contract package states each timing and trigger.
A tabletop exercise measures time from simulated detection to sponsor notice under 24 hours.
Notices are sent from a channel the sponsor can verify independently of email.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Echelon principal sanctions screening and ownership disclosure
statement: Echelon SHALL screen its owners, officers, personnel and contractors against OFAC lists at engagement and on list change, SHALL determine its own ownership for the OFAC 50 percent rule, and SHALL disclose beneficial owners to customers on request.
rationale: OFAC binds Echelon directly as a US person (strict liability). The baseline screens donors, advisors and grantees (CNV-GRT-006) but not Echelon itself.
acceptance_criteria: Screening records exist for every principal and contractor with list version and date.
An ownership statement is approved by the governing body.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Article 4A security procedure allocation
statement: Each program role table SHALL record the commercially reasonable security procedure between the sponsor and its bank for every payment order Unbound prepares, the party that authenticates the instruction, and the contractual allocation of loss for unauthorized orders among sponsor, bank and Unbound.
rationale: Batch 1 found the UCC 4A security procedure unaddressed. Because the sponsor originates and Unbound prepares, a sponsor will ask who bears loss for a fraudulent instruction transmitted through Unbound.
acceptance_criteria: The role table schema contains security procedure, authenticating party and loss allocation fields.
Rail activation (RailGoLive) fails when the fields are empty.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Vendor relationship and related-party disclosure
statement: Echelon SHALL maintain and disclose to each sponsor any board, committee, staff, fee-sharing, referral or financial relationship between Echelon, its owners or personnel and the sponsor, its advisors or its investment managers, and SHALL support the sponsor in identifying interested-person transactions.
rationale: CNV-GRT-009 controls payments from funds to related parties but no requirement covers Echelon itself as a related party. Batch 1 notes board-vendor overlap is documented in the DAF market.
acceptance_criteria: A conflict-of-interest register exists and is attested annually by every principal.
Each sponsor receives a disclosure statement before contract signature.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Encryption at rest for every store
statement: All Unbound data stores, including databases, object storage, search indexes, queues, logs, backups and replicas, SHALL be encrypted at rest with AES-256 or stronger using keys managed under DD-UNB-SEC-003, and an automated check SHALL fail deployment of any unencrypted store.
rationale: The baseline mentions encryption only in passing (SOC2-014 "defined and enforced", UNB-TEN-006 for dedicated databases); no requirement states encryption at rest, algorithm or coverage. This is a near-universal critical questionnaire item.
acceptance_criteria: An inventory of stores shows encryption status and key reference for 100 percent of stores.
An infrastructure-as-code policy test rejects an unencrypted store.
Backups and replicas are included in the inventory.
verification_method: Policy-as-code test plus monthly coverage report.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Encryption in transit
statement: All external connections SHALL use TLS 1.2 or later with TLS 1.3 preferred and legacy protocols disabled, and all internal connections between application, database, cache, queue and managed services SHALL use TLS with server certificate verification.
rationale: No baseline record specifies transport encryption except "secure transport" for custodian integrations (UNB-CUST-017).
acceptance_criteria: An external TLS scan shows no protocol below TLS 1.2.
Database connections reject non-TLS clients (server-side enforcement).
A code analyzer flags any disabled certificate validation.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Key management decision and controls
statement: Unbound SHALL resolve ADR-006 by recording a key management design that names the key service, key hierarchy, per-tenant key scope, rotation periods, dual control for destruction, separation between key administrators and data administrators, and logging of every key operation.
rationale: Key management appears only as a list item in UNB-TEN-008; ADR-006 (unbound@9b38de47:architecture/TENANT-AWARE-PERSISTENCE-DESIGN.md line 157) is unresolved. Crypto-shredding for erasure and exit (UNB-DATA-007, RR-UNB-TEN-016-r1) depends on it.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-006 is recorded with the listed elements.
A key inventory export shows owner, scope and rotation date for every key.
A test shows a single administrator cannot both read tenant data and destroy its key.
verification_method: Architecture review plus key operation log inspection.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Field-level protection of financial identifiers
statement: Bank account numbers, routing-account pairs, taxpayer identification numbers and Social Security numbers SHALL be stored only in the PII vault, encrypted or tokenized at field level, masked by default in every interface and export, and SHALL never appear in immutable ledger events, logs or AI prompts.
rationale: CNV-ARC-001 requires PII vault references in event payloads but no requirement names the fields, the protection method or masking. Batch 1 found no requirement to render stored ACH account numbers unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: A static analysis of event schemas shows no field typed as a financial identifier outside the vault.
A log and prompt scanner run on test traffic finds zero unmasked identifiers.
Unmasking requires a recorded purpose and is logged.
verification_method: Property-based tests plus scanner run per release.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Secrets management and secret scanning
statement: Application secrets, credentials and certificates SHALL be held only in a managed secret store with access by workload identity, rotated on a defined schedule and on personnel change, and every repository, build log and container image SHALL be scanned for secrets on each change with a blocking gate.

source_refs.locator: secret scanning not run in portfolio CI

rationale: Credential rotation appears only for integrations (UNB-API-STD-005). Tutela records that no portfolio repository runs secret scanning beyond its own self-scan.
acceptance_criteria: No secret value is present in configuration files in the repository.
The CI gate blocks a planted test secret.
Rotation records exist for every secret within its period.
verification_method: CI gate test plus rotation report.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Vulnerability management program with remediation targets
statement: Unbound SHALL operate a vulnerability management program covering application dependencies, the .NET runtime, container and operating system images and managed services, with remediation targets from discovery of 7 days for known-exploited vulnerabilities, 15 days for critical, 30 days for high and 90 days for medium, a time-limited exception process, and quarterly performance reporting.
rationale: SOC2-016 requires recording findings but sets no scope, timing or exception rule; it is the only vulnerability requirement in the baseline. The numeric targets are research recommendations pending owner decision (batch 1).
acceptance_criteria: A vulnerability register shows discovery date, severity, target and closure for each finding.
A quarterly report shows percentage remediated within target.
Every overdue finding has an approved, expiring exception.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend). Recurring: about 0.1 FTE.

title: Vulnerability disclosure policy
statement: Echelon SHALL publish a vulnerability disclosure policy with safe harbor language reviewed by counsel, a monitored security contact and a security.txt file on every Unbound domain, and SHALL acknowledge external reports within three business days.
rationale: Batch 1 found no VDP, SECURITY.md or security.txt in any Echelon repository and no requirement for one.
acceptance_criteria: security.txt is reachable at the well-known path with a current expiry.
A test report sent to the contact is acknowledged within three business days.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Independent penetration testing before real donor data
statement: An independent firm SHALL perform an authenticated application, API and infrastructure penetration test of the production-equivalent environment before any pilot with real donor data and at least annually and after major architecture change, with scope including every role, cross-tenant access attempts, business logic abuse of grant and payment controls, embedded components and AI interfaces, and remediation retest.
rationale: SOC2-016 mentions penetration testing only as a program to record. No requirement sets timing, independence or scope, and the coverage screen classed PEN as having no Unbound requirement for 29 of 32 questions.
acceptance_criteria: A letter of attestation names the firm, dates, scope and finding counts by severity.
Scope documentation shows cross-tenant and business-logic test cases.
All critical and high findings are retested and closed before the pilot.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend). Recurring: annual test, order of $20,000 to $60,000 (judgment).

title: Security scanning gates in the build
statement: Every Unbound build SHALL run dependency vulnerability and license scanning, secret scanning, infrastructure-as-code and container scanning and schema-driven API testing, and SHALL run F# rule analyzers for the Secure Construction Standard prohibitions in place of general SAST, with results normalized and blocking at agreed thresholds.
rationale: Batch 1 verified that no mature SAST parses F#; language-independent tools apply. The baseline has one scanning reference (UNB-XIN-OTH-004). Assessors will ask what scans F# code; the honest answer requires compensating analyzers.
acceptance_criteria: The pipeline definition contains each listed scanner with a blocking threshold.
A coverage matrix states which weakness classes each tool covers and which are covered only by design constraints.
A seeded vulnerable commit fails the gate.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Adopted secure development standard with enforced review
statement: Echelon SHALL formally adopt a secure development standard for Unbound mapped to NIST SSDF, and SHALL enforce branch protection so that no change, including one authored by an AI agent or an administrator, merges to a protected branch or deploys without review by at least one qualified human other than the author, with two non-author approvers for control-relevant modules per CNV-PLT-010.
rationale: The Secure Construction Standard v0.1 is proposed, not adopted, and has no AI rule. CNV-PLT-010 requires two approvers for control-relevant modules but no requirement covers other modules, AI-authored changes or administrator bypass. Branch protection on Echelon repositories is unknown.
acceptance_criteria: A signed adoption record exists.
Repository settings export shows required reviews, no administrator bypass and status checks on protected branches.
A sample of 25 merged changes shows a non-author human reviewer on each.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Release SBOM and signed provenance
statement: Each Unbound release SHALL produce an SBOM in SPDX or CycloneDX generated from resolved build dependencies including browser-delivered code, and signed build provenance, and deployment SHALL verify the signature before release to production.
rationale: CNV-PLT-010 requires signed builds and CNV-GOV-009 requires an SBOM license check, but no requirement states SBOM content, format or deployment verification. DD-ARC-002 found no Echelon release carries an SBOM; signing exists only in parts of Praxis and Strata.
acceptance_criteria: Each release artifact has an SBOM and provenance attestation.
An unsigned artifact is refused by the deployment step in a test.
verification_method: Release inspection and negative deployment test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Threat models as normative release gates
statement: Unbound SHALL maintain a threat model for every command class, external integration, webhook and embedded surface, reviewed at each material change, and a release SHALL be blocked when a changed component lacks a current threat model.
rationale: UNB-GAP-029 calls for threat models but is classified research-hypothesis, so it is not binding.
acceptance_criteria: A threat model record exists for each listed element with a review date after its last material change.
The release gate fails a test change to an unmodeled component.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Application security verification baseline
statement: Unbound SHALL verify each release against OWASP ASVS Level 2, including prohibition of dynamic evaluation facilities reachable from user, partner or AI input, secure session and cookie configuration, CSRF protection, output encoding and file intake controls, and SHALL record the result per requirement.
rationale: The coverage screen found 39 of 60 APP questions with no Unbound requirement. The Secure Construction Standard rules SEC-UI and SEC-EXEC are proposed only.
acceptance_criteria: An ASVS verification matrix exists per release with pass, fail or not-applicable and evidence per item.
No Level 2 item is failing at release without an expiring exception.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Security log retention and tamper evidence
statement: Unbound SHALL retain security and audit logs in a store separate from production with tamper-evident integrity verification for a retention period approved by counsel and the qualified auditor (proposed default: one year online, seven years archive for incident evidence), with legal hold support.
rationale: SOC2-023 forbids inventing a universal retention period; no requirement sets one, so the answer to retention questions is currently unknown. CNV-PLT-009 sets service-organization evidence retention but not security logs.
acceptance_criteria: A retention decision record exists signed by counsel and the auditor.
An integrity verification job detects a deleted log record in a test.
Production administrators cannot delete log records (negative test).
verification_method: Configuration test plus integrity verification run.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Runtime security monitoring and detection
statement: Unbound SHALL operate runtime security monitoring with a detection catalog covering authentication abuse, cross-tenant probing, privileged access, configuration change, ledger integrity failure and anomalous payment preparation, with alert routing to a named responder and coverage outside business hours.
rationale: Specified monitoring (MON-*) covers control evidence, not runtime threat detection, and DD-ARC-002 found no runtime security monitoring in any Echelon system (Vigila is a task organizer, Aegis is fault handling). This is an unverified Echelon capability dependency.
acceptance_criteria: A detection catalog lists each listed scenario with a test.
Synthetic tests trigger each detection and an alert reaches the on-call responder.
Missing-heartbeat alerts fire when a log source stops.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend). Recurring: tooling and on-call coverage.

title: Approved incident response plan and exercises
statement: Echelon SHALL approve an incident response plan for Unbound naming the incident lead and backup, severity classes, customer and regulator notification steps, evidence preservation, breach counsel and forensic retainer, and SHALL exercise it at least annually with scenarios including ransomware, compromised AI agent and payment instruction tampering.
rationale: Incident response appears only as list items (UNB-OPS-001, SOC2-015) and a research-hypothesis gap (UNB-GAP-034). No plan owner, retainer or breach counsel exists.
acceptance_criteria: An approved plan exists with the listed elements.
An exercise report with timeline and corrective actions exists within the last 12 months.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend). Recurring: retainer fees unknown.

title: Workforce access lifecycle with revocation targets
statement: All workforce access, including cloud consoles, code hosting, secret stores, AI tool accounts and production databases, SHALL be provisioned through recorded requests, reviewed quarterly and revoked within 4 hours of involuntary and 24 hours of voluntary departure, with phishing-resistant authentication per CNV-PLT-003.
rationale: CNV-PLT-003 governs authenticator strength; SOC2-010 lists deprovisioning but sets no time. The revocation targets are judgment and need owner approval.
acceptance_criteria: A deprovisioning report shows time to revoke per departure against target.
A quarterly recertification record exists for each system.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Personnel security program
statement: Echelon SHALL perform FCRA-compliant background checks before granting access to customer data or production, require signed confidentiality and acceptable-use agreements, and deliver role-based security, fraud-awareness and secure development training at onboarding and annually, for employees and contractors.
rationale: The baseline has no personnel security requirement. Batch 1 found Fidelity supplier policies require deep background checks.
acceptance_criteria: Screening, agreement and training completion records exist for every person with access.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend). Recurring: per-hire screening fees.

title: Workforce endpoint security
statement: Every device used to access Unbound production, code hosting or customer data SHALL be managed, encrypted, patched within defined periods and protected by endpoint detection and response, and unmanaged devices SHALL be denied by conditional access.
rationale: Workforce devices are unknown and no requirement covers them; cyber insurers and bank suppliers ask about EDR.
acceptance_criteria: Device inventory reconciles to personnel.
A login attempt from an unmanaged device is denied in a test.
verification_method: Conditional access test plus compliance report.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend). Recurring: per-device licensing.

title: Information security program charter and qualified individual
statement: Echelon SHALL adopt a written information security program covering Unbound, approved by its governing body, designate a qualified individual responsible for it with direct reporting to that body, maintain a policy register with owners and review dates, and report to the governing body at least annually.
rationale: CNV-GOV-003 assumes a CISO with access to the audit committee, but no organizational requirement establishes the program. The only policy located is the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1.
acceptance_criteria: A signed program charter and qualified individual designation exist.
The policy register lists each policy with approval date.
An annual report to the governing body exists.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Hosting provider decision with shared responsibility
statement: Echelon SHALL record a hosting decision for Unbound naming the cloud provider, services, primary and recovery regions in the United States, the provider assurance reports reviewed with complementary user entity controls mapped, and a shared responsibility matrix, before architecture acceptance.
rationale: CNV-ARC-001 assumes managed PostgreSQL but no provider is chosen; TENANT-AWARE-PERSISTENCE-DESIGN ADR-001 leaves the engine unchosen. Twenty infrastructure decisions are open (batch 1). Hosting questions are answered unknown today.
acceptance_criteria: A decision record names provider, services and regions.
A provider SOC report review memo maps provider CUECs to Unbound controls.
A shared responsibility matrix covers every control in DD-UNB-GOV-003.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Cloud account guardrails and root credential custody
statement: Unbound cloud accounts SHALL separate production, non-production, logging and backup accounts, protect root credentials with hardware keys held under split custody, alert on every root use, and enforce preventive guardrails against public storage, disabled logging and unencrypted resources.
rationale: CNV-PLT-010 makes database administration break-glass with two-person activation but no requirement covers cloud account structure or root credentials; for a one-person organization split custody needs a named second holder.
acceptance_criteria: An account inventory shows separation.
A root login test generates an alert.
Guardrail denial tests pass.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Network exposure controls
statement: The database tier SHALL not be reachable from the internet or from any system other than the application tier and approved break-glass paths, outbound traffic SHALL be restricted to an allowlist, and public endpoints SHALL sit behind managed edge protection with rate limiting and DDoS mitigation.
rationale: The coverage screen found NET questions answered mostly by unrelated requirements; no requirement specifies network segmentation or egress control.
acceptance_criteria: An external attack surface scan shows no database endpoint.
An egress test to an unlisted host is denied.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Minimum independent personnel for control-relevant operations
statement: Before production, Echelon SHALL have at least two qualified people, neither able to act alone, for control-relevant code approval, production break-glass, key destruction and release signing, documenting any compensating control and its expiry while that condition is unmet.
rationale: CNV-PLT-010 requires two non-author approvers and two-person break-glass, and TVR-ORG-003-Q leaves small-scale compensation open. The answer units record that Echelon may have one human engineer (ANS-SDL-003). The product separation of duties design is unenforceable without people.
acceptance_criteria: A roster shows at least two qualified holders per listed function.
Any single-holder function has a documented, expiring compensating control approved by the governing body.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: high (over six person-months or over $50,000 external spend). Recurring: at least one additional qualified person.

title: Donor-facing privacy notice ownership in branded deployments
statement: Every donor-facing surface SHALL display the legal sponsor, the organization whose privacy notice governs the session and a link to that notice, and each program activation SHALL record which notice applies and who maintains it.
rationale: UNB-RCN-WF-009 requires a legal-sponsor disclosure at activation, but no requirement addresses which privacy notice governs a white-labeled session. A documented sponsor policy disclaims coverage of third-party branded services (DD-IND-DAF-001).
acceptance_criteria: Activation fails without a recorded governing notice.
A UI test confirms the notice link on every donor-facing page.
verification_method: UI test plus activation gate test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Processor role and data processing agreement
statement: Echelon SHALL act as processor or service provider for all sponsor personal data, SHALL publish a standard data processing agreement covering purpose limitation, subprocessor flow-down, assistance with rights requests, breach notice, deletion and audit, and SHALL list every purpose for which it uses customer data for its own benefit (expected: none beyond service delivery, security and billing).
rationale: UNB-TEN-008 lists data processing agreements as something to support per partner; no requirement fixes Echelon's role or terms. CCPA likely does not reach nonprofit sponsors but some state laws cover nonprofits, and for-profit partners need service-provider terms.
acceptance_criteria: A standard DPA exists reviewed by counsel.
A data use register lists each Echelon purpose.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Safeguards-equivalent program and GLBA applicability determination
statement: Echelon SHALL obtain a counsel determination of whether GLBA, the FTC Safeguards Rule or the Interagency Safeguards Guidelines apply to Echelon or reach it through customers, and regardless of the outcome SHALL commit contractually to safeguards equivalent to the FTC Safeguards Rule elements for donor and advisor data.
rationale: Batch 1 records the GLBA status of DAF sponsors and of Echelon as the largest open legal question (OQ-DD-POL-001); no Unbound requirement addresses it.
acceptance_criteria: A counsel memo states the determination.
An annual report against each Safeguards Rule element exists.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Rights requests against append-only records
statement: Unbound SHALL implement, after counsel review, a rights request workflow that verifies requester identity and authority, routes the decision to the sponsor as controller, and executes approved erasure by crypto-shredding vault entries while preserving records the law or the sponsor must retain, and SHALL state in customer materials what persists after erasure, including backups until expiry.
rationale: UNB-DATA-007 and UNB-IMM-008 state principles but defer the design; UNB-DATA-001 forbids deletion of authoritative events. Regulators may treat retained ciphertext as personal data (batch 1). Counsel resolution is required before production.
acceptance_criteria: A counsel memo approves the erasure method per record class.
A test erases a donor and verifies the vault entry is unrecoverable while ledger integrity verification still passes.
Customer materials list what persists.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: No sale, sharing or third-party tracking
statement: Unbound SHALL NOT sell or share personal data or use it for targeted advertising, SHALL NOT load third-party analytics, advertising, social or session replay scripts on authenticated pages, and SHALL enforce this with a content security policy and a build-time script inventory check, including on sponsor-branded pages.
rationale: No requirement prohibits tracking tags; answer units record the open question whether white-label sponsors will demand their own analytics tags (ANS-PRV-009).
acceptance_criteria: The script inventory check fails a build that adds an unlisted third-party script.
The CSP blocks third-party script origins on authenticated pages in a browser test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: United States data location and access origin
statement: Customer data, backups, logs, AI inference and support access SHALL remain in and originate from the United States unless a sponsor contract approves otherwise, and every access SHALL record its origin.
rationale: UNB-TEN-008 lists residency as something to support; no default exists. Large-bank supplier standards require US-only access (batch 1).
acceptance_criteria: A data location inventory shows US regions for every store and subprocessor.
Access logs carry origin.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Privacy impact assessment gate
statement: A privacy impact assessment SHALL be completed and approved before any feature introduces a new personal data category, purpose, recipient, AI processing of personal data or cross-sponsor aggregation, and the release gate SHALL check for it.
rationale: No PIA requirement exists. Answer units leave open whether cross-sponsor analytics will be pursued (ANS-PRV-006, ANS-PRV-012).
acceptance_criteria: A PIA register exists.
The release gate blocks a test change tagged as new data category without a PIA.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Privacy program owner
statement: Echelon SHALL designate a privacy officer accountable for the Unbound privacy program, the record of processing and rights request handling.
rationale: ANS-PRV-001 records the role as unassigned.
acceptance_criteria: A designation record exists.
A generated record of processing is reviewed by the officer quarterly.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: AI provider inventory and data terms
statement: Echelon SHALL maintain an inventory of every AI model provider and AI tool used to build, operate or deliver Unbound, and SHALL use for any customer data only provider tiers with contractual no-training commitments, zero or bounded retention, United States processing and listing as a subprocessor.
rationale: No requirement inventories AI providers or their terms; UNB-XIN-SAS-009 only meters model calls. Answer units for training and retention are unknown, and Echelon builds largely with AI coding agents.
acceptance_criteria: An inventory lists provider, model, tier, terms reference, retention, region and data classes.
A tool broker or egress control denies calls to unlisted AI endpoints in a test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: No training on customer data
statement: Echelon SHALL NOT use sponsor, donor, advisor or grantee data to train, fine-tune or evaluate models, prompts or agents without the sponsor's written opt-in per use, and SHALL state this in the contract.
rationale: Business plan 10.04 is boilerplate and states no position (batch 1); no Unbound requirement exists.
acceptance_criteria: The contract package contains the commitment.
Evaluation datasets are synthetic or opt-in, verified by dataset register.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: AI coding agent permissions and production isolation
statement: AI coding and operations agents SHALL run under their own identities with least privilege, SHALL NOT push to protected branches, approve changes, modify CI or security gate configuration, or access production data or secrets, and every agent action SHALL be attributable to an execution and accountable human.
rationale: CNV-AIO-001 governs AI in the product, not engineering agents. Answer units on agent branch permissions and review are unknown (ANS-AIS-008); Praxis attribution exists but identity is asserted, not cryptographically verified.
acceptance_criteria: An agent permission manifest exists per agent.
Negative tests show an agent token cannot merge, edit protected CI paths or read production.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: AI security testing before enabling AI features
statement: Before any AI feature is enabled for a sponsor, Unbound SHALL pass a versioned adversarial suite covering direct and indirect prompt injection, cross-tenant retrieval, tool misuse, parameter tampering and unsafe output handling, and SHALL repeat it on every model, prompt or tool change.
rationale: CNV-AIO-002 and UNB-AIO-003 state design boundaries; AIN-012 and UNB-GAP-033 are proposed or hypothesis. No test obligation or release gate exists.
acceptance_criteria: Suite results per release show zero unauthorized tool executions and zero cross-tenant disclosures.
The release gate blocks an AI change without a current suite run.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Model change and provider deprecation control
statement: Unbound SHALL pin model versions, receive or monitor provider deprecation notices, re-run evaluation and adversarial suites before any model change, notify sponsors of material model or provider changes in advance, and keep deterministic paths operable without AI.
rationale: CNV-AIO-001 requires AI unavailability not to stop deterministic paths; no requirement covers model version change.
acceptance_criteria: Model identifiers are pinned in configuration.
A change record shows suite results and sponsor notice before a model switch.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Automated decision applicability determination
statement: Echelon SHALL determine, with counsel, whether any Unbound AI or rules feature is a consequential or automated decision under applicable state law (including Colorado SB 26-189) and whether sponsors need notice or appeal mechanisms, and SHALL record the result per feature.
rationale: Batch 1 records the Colorado AI Act repealed and reenacted as an automated decision-making technology law with duties from 2027-01-01; CNV-GRT-012 provides decline reasons but no applicability analysis exists.
acceptance_criteria: A determination record exists for each AI or rules feature affecting individuals.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Single isolation default and dependent clause reconciliation
statement: Unbound SHALL record one architecture decision stating the default tenant isolation profile and the conditions for dedicated databases, and SHALL amend CNV-TEN-001, CNV-ARC-003 and RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 so that no clause depends on an unaccepted database-per-sponsor decision.
rationale: Verified contradiction: CNV-ARC-001 sets one shared cluster with schema and role per sponsor, RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 (adopted-provisional, not amended) sets dedicated database per tenant as the default, and CNV-TEN-001 and CNV-ARC-003 each still state that they depend on acceptance of the database-per-sponsor architecture decision, although both also describe the shared-cluster case. Tenant isolation is the first architecture question every assessor asks.
acceptance_criteria: One decision record names the default profile.
CNV-TEN-001 and CNV-ARC-003 no longer state a dependency on an unaccepted decision.
RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1 is flagged in the DD-UNB-GOV-001 register.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Independent verification of tenant isolation
statement: The tenant isolation suite (negative tests across database, cache, search, queue, AI retrieval, exports and embedded widgets) SHALL run on every release and be included in the independent penetration test scope, with continuous cross-tenant canary probes in production.
rationale: Negative isolation tests are required at activation (UNB-RCN-WF-009) and in CNV-ARC-001, but no requirement covers continuous production canaries or independent testing.
acceptance_criteria: Suite results per release show zero cross-tenant reads.
Canary telemetry shows probe executions daily with zero leaks.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Custom domains and certificate management
statement: Unbound SHALL support sponsor and partner custom domains with automated certificate issuance and renewal, domain ownership verification, HSTS, certificate expiry monitoring and removal on partner exit.
rationale: ANS-WLB-001 records that custom domain and TLS certificate management for white-label portals is not specified.
acceptance_criteria: A domain cannot be bound without verification.
Certificates renew automatically in a test with a short-lived certificate.
Exit removes the domain binding.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Embedded component security contract
statement: Unbound SHALL decide the embedding mechanism (ADR-M-03) and specify for every embedded component: per-partner frame-ancestors allowlist, single-use launch tokens with a lifetime of at most 60 seconds bound to origin and user, independent authentication and authorization by Unbound, validated message schemas for host communication, overlay-resistant confirmation for consequential actions and session behavior under third-party cookie restrictions.
rationale: INT-015 and AIN-029 are one-line Proposed table rows; Limen lacks element or shadow-root roots so ADR-M-03 is unresolved and the interim iframe or web-component approach sits uneasily with SEC-UI-002 (batch 1, verified in 07-ECHELON-CAPABILITY-ASSESSMENT.md line 148). The 60-second value is judgment.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-M-03 is recorded.
Adversarial tests show framing from an unlisted origin fails, a replayed token fails and a host-asserted identity is not trusted.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Brand attribution rule for white-label surfaces
statement: Unbound SHALL state where Unbound and Echelon attribution appears on sponsor-branded surfaces, reconciling UNB-EXP-002 with the Brand Kit model so that the legal sponsor is always identified and vendor attribution never implies vendor control of funds.
rationale: UNB-EXP-002 requires independent Unbound branding with Echelon attribution while REQ-X-030 and CNV-EXP-001 describe sponsor Brand Kits and an Echelon default theme; the attribution rule for white-label surfaces is not stated.
acceptance_criteria: A rule exists and Brand Kit validation enforces it.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Partner API authentication standard
statement: Partner and integration API access SHALL use OAuth 2.0 client credentials with private-key JWT or mutual TLS and sender-constrained tokens; static API keys SHALL NOT authorize money-affecting, authority-affecting or bulk export operations, and sponsors SHALL see and revoke every credential for their tenant.
rationale: No baseline record names an API authentication method (zero matches for OAuth or mTLS); UNB-API-STD-005 requires only documentation. An answer unit notes integrations may only support static keys.
acceptance_criteria: The API gateway rejects a static key on a money-affecting route in a test.
A sponsor credential list shows every client for its tenant.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Developer documentation, changelog and sandbox
statement: Unbound SHALL publish versioned API documentation with schemas, a security changelog, an isolated sandbox that cannot send real payments, and the deprecation lifecycle required by CNV-EXP-001.
rationale: CNV-EXP-001 sets an 18-month breaking-change notice and CNV-AIO-001 requires machine-readable assistance, but no requirement establishes a sandbox or public changelog. The sponsor audit matrix (C06, C22) asks for repeatable sandbox evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation and changelog are published per version.
A sandbox payment attempt is refused by rail configuration.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Per-tenant rate and business-flow limits in release 1
statement: Rate limits per client, user and tenant, and business-flow limits on recommendation, contribution form and export endpoints, SHALL be in release 1 rather than deferred, and SHALL be returned in response metadata.
rationale: RR-UNB-API-STD-003-r1 (rate limits per tier and tenant) is unvalidated and deferred; r2 is proposed. Public contribution forms need abuse controls regardless of card deferral.
acceptance_criteria: Load tests show throttling per tenant without affecting other tenants.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Scheduled and recurring contributions model
statement: Unbound SHALL either define scheduled and recurring contributions (mandate record, cadence, amount, funding source, authorization evidence under Nacha and Regulation E where applicable, revocation, failure handling and expected-versus-received reconciliation) or record their exclusion from release 1 in customer materials.
rationale: The baseline has no requirement for scheduled or recurring contributions (zero matches), and the question bank has no dedicated question; CNV-FIN-003 states release 1 has no donor ACH debit origination. Sponsors offering automatic giving will ask.
acceptance_criteria: Either a mandate lifecycle specification with acceptance tests exists, or customer materials state the exclusion.
If implemented, a revoked mandate produces no further expected contributions in a test.
verification_method: Specification review or customer material review.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Reconciliation sampling method and break reporting
statement: Unbound SHALL specify the error-bound sampling method used for attestation of auto-passed reconciliation items, default break aging thresholds and escalation, and a sponsor-facing break report with frequency and content.
rationale: CNV-FIN-004 leaves sample size to the controller and labels numeric values illustrative; ANS-RCN-003 and ANS-RCN-005 record that break reporting and the sampling method are unspecified.
acceptance_criteria: A documented method computes sample size from an error bound and confidence level.
A sponsor break report sample shows aging, attribution and owner.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Advance notice of fee changes
statement: A fee schedule version that increases any charge to a fund or donor SHALL NOT take effect until a sponsor-set notice period (default 30 days) has elapsed after notice to affected donors and the sponsor, and the notice SHALL be recorded.
rationale: ANS-FEE-003 records no requirement for advance notice of fee increases. CNV-FIN-002 versions schedules but has no notice rule. The 30-day default is judgment.
acceptance_criteria: Activation of a higher fee version before the notice period fails in a test.
Notice delivery records exist for each affected donor.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Information return applicability
statement: Unbound SHALL determine, with counsel, which payments it prepares may require Form 1099 information returns (for example payments to non-charity payees, refunds or vendor fees netted from proceeds), collect taxpayer identification where required, and export the data for the sponsor's filing.
rationale: No requirement mentions Form 1099 (zero matches). The relevant IRS instructions are not yet in the source register (batch 1 unseeded list).
acceptance_criteria: A determination record exists per payment type.
An export produces payee, TIN status and amount for flagged payments.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).
notes: Source gap: IRS General Instructions for Certain Information Returns should be added to sources before acceptance.

title: Ledger integrity anchoring mechanism
statement: Unbound SHALL select and benchmark the ledger integrity mechanism required by UNB-DATA-012 and CNV-PLT-010 (hash chain with signed checkpoints anchored daily outside Echelon-controlled infrastructure) and SHALL provide a sponsor-runnable verifier.
rationale: CNV-PLT-010 requires daily external anchoring and UNB-DATA-012 leaves the mechanism undecided. ANS-ENC-012 records the anchor location as open. Evidence signing exists only partially in Echelon (DD-ARC-002).
acceptance_criteria: A decision record names the mechanism and anchor location.
The verifier detects a deleted, altered, duplicated and reordered record in tests, including after restore.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Complementary user entity controls published per sponsor
statement: Before a sponsor relies on Unbound for financial reporting, Unbound SHALL publish to that sponsor a list of complementary user entity controls derived from its configuration and SHALL keep the list current on configuration change, in release 1 rather than deferred.
rationale: Verified: UNB-XIN-ACC-009 requires the CUEC list but its release scope is Deferred, while CNV-GOV-001 requires CUECs to be mapped before live reliance. Sponsor auditors need the list before the first close.
acceptance_criteria: A CUEC list exists for each activated sponsor with configuration version.
Each convergence clause with cuec true maps to a CUEC entry.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Resolve sponsor-pool NAV and unitization scope
statement: Unbound SHALL mark UNB-NAV-*, UNB-INV-003, UNB-INV-004 and UNB-INV-022 as superseded or narrow them to fund-level valuations derived from external manager or custodian inputs, consistent with CNV-LEG-001 and CNV-FIN-005, and customer materials SHALL state that Unbound does not operate sponsor-maintained investment pools.
rationale: Verified contradiction: CNV-LEG-001 states no sponsor-maintained investment pools SHALL be offered, while UNB-INV-003 (pooled vehicles with unit prices, subscriptions and redemptions), UNB-INV-022 and 53 UNB-NAV records remain original and unamended. An assessor reading UNB-NAV would conclude Unbound computes NAV for sponsor pools.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed record is flagged or amended.
A search of customer materials finds no claim of pool NAV operation.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Remove trade execution APIs
statement: Unbound SHALL NOT expose any API or workflow that submits, routes or executes securities orders for fund accounts; UNB-CUST-007 SHALL be amended to limit Unbound to relaying donor allocation recommendations and recording manager or custodian execution status.
rationale: Verified contradiction: UNB-CUST-007 (original, unamended) says execution APIs require separately validated contractual permissions and human authority, while CNV-LEG-001 prohibits routing orders for others' accounts. ANS-CUS-005 records the conflict.
acceptance_criteria: UNB-CUST-007 is amended or flagged.
An API inventory shows no order submission endpoint.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Custodian integration certification
statement: Activation of a custodian integration SHALL require recorded data licensing and entitlement terms, authenticated file or API origin, freshness and gap detection, raw feed retention, a complementary user entity control assignment from the custodian SOC report and a completed recovery drill.
rationale: Requirements exist piecemeal but no custodian is selected and no activation gate binds them (ANS-CUS-001, ANS-CUS-006).
acceptance_criteria: The activation gate fails when any listed element is missing.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Non-cash gift substantiation requirements
statement: Unbound SHALL replace the research-hypothesis gaps UNB-GAP-011 and UNB-GAP-012 with normative requirements for Form 8283 Part V acknowledgment support, Form 8282 disposition tracking within three years, separation of donor-claimed value, appraisal value and sponsor accounting value, and acknowledgment wording that describes rather than values non-cash property.
rationale: UNB-GAP-011 and UNB-GAP-012 are classified research-hypothesis. CNV-GRT-013 requires an intermediary that sells on receipt and records the acknowledgment and sale, but detailed substantiation requirements are missing (ANS-CON-004).
acceptance_criteria: Normative requirements with acceptance tests exist for each listed element.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).
notes: Source gap: IRS Form 8283 and 8282 instructions are not in the source register.

title: Payment file and channel security
statement: Payment instructions and files SHALL be generated in the sponsor cell, signed and encrypted for transmission to the bank or rail over an authenticated channel named per rail, credentials for bank channels SHALL be held in the secret store under workload identity, and the bank SHALL be able to verify origin.
rationale: Batch 1 found payment file encryption and signing unspecified; transport depends on unselected banks (ANS-PAY-007).
acceptance_criteria: A per-rail record names transport, encryption and signing.
A tampered file is rejected by the verification step in a test.
verification_method: Integration test with bank test environment.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Nacha account number protection
statement: Stored ACH account numbers SHALL be rendered unreadable at rest as required for third-party service providers by the Nacha supplementing data security requirements, independent of volume thresholds.
rationale: CNV-PAY-001 accepts TPSP obligations by contract; no requirement implements this one (batch 1). Applying it regardless of volume avoids a later threshold analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A data scan of non-vault stores finds no readable account number.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Nacha risk-based fraud monitoring program
statement: Unbound SHALL operate, as a TPSP, a documented risk-based fraud monitoring program for entries it prepares (detection of false pretenses, account takeover and anomalous destinations, review cadence, escalation to the sponsor and ODFI, and annual review), with rules versioned and evidence retained.
rationale: Batch 1: Nacha phase 2 (effective June 2026) applies risk-based fraud monitoring to all TPSPs regardless of volume; this is a direct, in-force obligation. CNV-PAY-001 accepts it by contract but no requirement defines the program.
acceptance_criteria: A program document with rules, owners and review cadence exists.
Synthetic anomalous entries generate cases.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Emergency payments during an Unbound outage
statement: Unbound SHALL define and test with each sponsor a procedure for urgent grants during an Unbound outage, in which the sponsor pays through its own bank channel with sanctions, eligibility and dual approval performed manually against a recorded snapshot, and every such payment is reconciled back into the platform before dispatch resumes.
rationale: TVR-PAY-004-Q (emergency payments during outage) is an open question; CNV-PLT-007 guarantees the sponsor can pay through its own bank but no procedure or snapshot exists.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook exists per sponsor.
An exercise shows a manually paid grant reconciled and not re-dispatched.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Check production custody
statement: For the check fallback rail, Unbound SHALL specify who prints and mails checks, custody of check stock and signature images, positive pay file delivery timing and controls preventing a vendor or printer from altering payee or amount.
rationale: CNV-PAY-002 covers check lifecycle and positive pay and UNB-XIN-OTH-004 requires print batch manifests and per-piece dispositions from the print vendor; check stock custody, signature image custody and controls against vendor alteration remain unspecified, and CNV-PAY-001 makes a check fallback mandatory for every program.
acceptance_criteria: A check operations specification exists.
Positive pay issue files are produced before release in a test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: End-to-end idempotency for ACH
statement: Because ACH lacks an end-to-end idempotency key, Unbound SHALL bind each entry to a stable trace or identification value recorded before transmission and SHALL resolve unknown outcomes only through rail status queries or bank activity matching before any re-initiation.
rationale: TVR-PAY-002-Q records that ACH lacks an end-to-end key; CNV-PAY-004 governs unknown outcomes. The binding of a stable identifier is not stated.
acceptance_criteria: A replay test after crash produces no duplicate entry.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Production sanctions matcher and list provider
statement: Before activation, Unbound SHALL select a sanctions list provider and matcher, validate it against the versioned perturbation suite required by CNV-GRT-006 with recall approved by each sponsor compliance officer, and record subgroup false-alert rates.
rationale: Verified: CNV-GRT-006 states the reference matcher does not meet the recall test and SHALL NOT be used in production; no replacement or provider is selected.
acceptance_criteria: A validation report shows recall on the suite meeting the approved target.
Subgroup false-alert rates are reported.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend). Recurring: list data subscription.

title: Adverse media in grantee diligence
statement: Unbound SHALL define whether and how adverse media is used in grantee deep review, including sources, licensing, human review and the rule that adverse media is input for a qualified reviewer, never an automatic decline.
rationale: No requirement mentions adverse media (zero matches). CNV-GRT-003 requires any known adverse public fact to be considered but names no source.
acceptance_criteria: A policy records the decision.
If used, review records show source, date and reviewer.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: State charity standing beyond California
statement: Unbound SHALL define a plan and data sources to extend state charity standing checks beyond California, prioritized by sponsor grant volume, and SHALL display the coverage limits to reviewers.
rationale: CNV-GRT-015 covers California first; other states are unspecified.
acceptance_criteria: A coverage table lists states with source and status.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Expenditure responsibility handling in release 1
statement: Until an expenditure responsibility workflow exists, Unbound SHALL block grants to recipients that would require expenditure responsibility and SHALL tell the recommender why.
rationale: CNV-GRT-008 (intermediaries and equivalency determinations) is deferred and batch 1 found the expenditure responsibility workflow unspecified; CNV-GRT-002 defines eligible classes but the blocking behavior for ER-requiring grants is not explicit.
acceptance_criteria: A grant to a non-public-charity recipient class requiring ER is refused in a test with a neutral reason.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Death and incapacity verification sources and executor access
statement: Unbound SHALL specify acceptable evidence and sources for verifying a donor's death or incapacity, the verification steps before authority changes, and what an executor or estate representative may see and do.
rationale: CNV-ENT-001 and AUTH-I5 cover suspension and succession, but batch 1 found death-verification sources and executor visibility unspecified; UNB-GAP-015 is a research hypothesis.
acceptance_criteria: A specification lists evidence types and verification steps.
An executor role test shows read-only access limited to the deceased donor's funds.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Support model, severity matrix and status page
statement: Unbound SHALL define support hours and after-hours coverage for critical issues, a severity matrix with response and update targets, an escalation matrix, a status page hosted independently of production with component status and incident history, and maintenance notice periods.
rationale: UNB-GAP-028 (support coverage, SLAs, escalation) is a research hypothesis; CNV-ARC-001 forbids numeric contractual SLAs before benchmark and pilot evidence, so targets must be published as objectives until then.
acceptance_criteria: A published support policy and severity matrix exist.
The status page remains available when production is down in a test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend). Recurring: on-call coverage.

title: Consent-based support access to donor accounts
statement: Support access to a donor or advisor account SHALL require sponsor-policy approval and, where the sponsor notice requires it, recorded user consent, SHALL be time-bounded and read-only by default, and SHALL be visible to the sponsor and the user afterward.
rationale: CNV-ARC-002 requires sponsor pre-approval and evidence for operator access; at least one sponsor privacy notice describes user consent for vendor support login (DD-IND-DAF-001), which no requirement captures.
acceptance_criteria: A support session without consent is refused where the sponsor requires consent.
The access transparency log shows the session to the sponsor.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Manual intervention register
statement: Every manual operator action that can affect a sponsor's data, holds or instruction flow (break-glass, data correction, hold placement, replay, export on request) SHALL be listed in a register with permitted roles, approvals, evidence and sponsor visibility, and any action not on the register SHALL be technically blocked.
rationale: CNV-GOV-006 justifies human steps in the sponsor workflow and CNV-PLT-007 governs platform holds, but operator interventions are spread across clauses with no single register an assessor can review.
acceptance_criteria: The register exists and maps each action to its governing clause.
An unregistered administrative command is rejected in a test.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Key-person continuity
statement: Echelon SHALL document a succession arrangement naming a person with legal authority to act if the principal is unavailable, emergency custody of credentials for domains, code hosting, cloud accounts and signing keys, and a key-person dependency register with mitigations.
rationale: ANS-BCP-005 records unknown how many people can deploy, restore or rotate credentials and whether a succession arrangement exists. For a founder-led company this is a deciding question.
acceptance_criteria: A signed succession designation exists.
An emergency credential custody record exists and a test recovery by the designee succeeds.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Business continuity program
statement: Echelon SHALL adopt a business continuity policy and business impact analysis for Unbound, plans with out-of-band communication, and an annual exercise program including a sponsor-participating exercise.
rationale: Continuity appears only as list items (UNB-OPS-001, SOC2-015) and a hypothesis (UNB-GAP-028).
acceptance_criteria: Approved policy and BIA exist.
An exercise report with remediation exists within 12 months.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Approved recovery objectives and restore tests
statement: Unbound SHALL approve the single recovery objectives table required by CNV-ARC-001 (keyed by data class and isolation profile), retire the per-capability wording of UNB-RES-003, and demonstrate the objectives by failover and restore tests before production.
rationale: Verified: UNB-RES-003 (original, not amended) requires RTO and RPO per capability while CNV-ARC-001 requires one table keyed by data class; RR-UNB-RES-003-r2 values are candidates only. Recovery objective questions cannot be answered.
acceptance_criteria: An approved table exists.
A restore test report shows measured RTO and RPO against the table and post-restore payment safety checks.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Rebuild from source after account compromise
statement: Unbound SHALL be able to rebuild production in a clean cloud account from source, infrastructure code and immutable backups held in a separate account, and SHALL test this at least annually.
rationale: The coverage screen classed DDQ-DR-0016 as only weakly covered; UNB-GAP-034 (immutable backup, restoration tests) is a hypothesis.
acceptance_criteria: A rebuild test report shows time to rebuild and integrity verification passing.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Accessibility conformance report with independent validation
statement: Unbound SHALL publish an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT, WCAG 2.2 and Section 508 editions) for each major release covering every user role and surface, validated by an independent accessibility specialist, with defect remediation targets by severity.
rationale: CNV-EXP-001 requires WCAG 2.2 AA and measured conformance before publication, but no requirement produces an ACR or independent validation; a large-bank supplier policy does not accept self-assessment.
acceptance_criteria: An ACR exists per release with preparer and validator named.
A defect register shows remediation against targets.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend). Recurring: per-release validation.

title: Accessible PDF pipeline
statement: Unbound SHALL select a PDF renderer that produces tagged PDF conforming to PDF/UA for statements, acknowledgments and grant letters, verify it with automated and manual checks, and amend UNB-PLAT-003 to match CNV-EXP-001.
rationale: Verified: UNB-PLAT-003 requires Folio for all enterprise documents, while CNV-EXP-001 states Folio provides markup only and the PDF pipeline is Unbound-owned until an upstream renderer exists. Folio does not provide tagged PDF (batch 1). No renderer is chosen.
acceptance_criteria: A renderer decision record exists.
PDF/UA validation passes for each document template.
verification_method: Automated PDF/UA validation plus screen reader check.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: medium (one to six person-months or $10,000 to $50,000 external spend).

title: Accessibility legal applicability
statement: Echelon SHALL obtain a determination of which accessibility laws apply through its intended customers (ADA Title III, Title II for public entities, Section 508, European Accessibility Act) and record contractual commitments accordingly.
rationale: UNB-GAP-031 (assess applicable ADA obligations) is a research hypothesis; ANS-A11Y-007 records customer-type questions open.
acceptance_criteria: A determination record exists.
cost_impact: Judgment, order of magnitude, not sourced: low (under one person-month of effort or under $10,000 external spend).

title: Accessible authentication and identity proofing
statement: Sign-in, step-up and identity proofing SHALL be completable without cognitive function tests, puzzles or sole reliance on visual or biometric steps, using the AccessibleAssurancePath of CNV-PLT-011, verified by assistive technology testing.
